blocks.text: The site grading design for {{fact:f:E-2001-001.client}} is on schedule at the midpoint and remains within the fixed design fee of {{fact:f:E-2001-001.fee}}. The preliminary grading is essentially complete, and the set is now in coordination with the roadway and drainage sheets.

This report covers the current period on the Esparza-Lamb set. It summarizes what was finished, what comes next, and the items that could affect the schedule. It is written for the client, and it is deliberately short.

Design is roughly half complete and tracking to plan. No change to scope or fee is anticipated. The work continues to draw from the survey and from our own field observations, and the set is being kept coordinated as it develops. Contours, elevations, and drainage are checked against one another as they are drawn, so the set does not have to be reconciled all at once near the end. The half that remains is of the same kind as the half now done, so there is no part of the work still ahead that we have not already handled on this set.

The preliminary grading plans and finished elevations were completed and checked against the roadway profile. Jason Jordan brought the roadway and site base sheets to the same stage, so the two sets can now be reviewed together rather than in isolation. The drainage details were advanced toward final, and the inlet callouts flagged at the last meeting were corrected to match the details they reference.

The earthwork was taken from a first cut-and-fill pass, and the quantities are close enough now to confirm that the site balances without an unusual import or export of material. A supplemental survey shot was taken at the entrance, and the finished grade there now rests on measured ground rather than on an interpolation.

The project folder was brought fully current. Every sheet is tied to the memorandum that governs it, revisions are clouded and logged, and the standard details in use were confirmed to be the current issue. A clean, coordinated review copy of the set is now being assembled for the client.

The next period completes the grading set and the earthwork quantities and closes out the drainage details. Jason Jordan will finish the roadway and site sheets in parallel, so the whole package advances together. A coordinated review copy will then go to the client, ahead of the review that precedes sealing and issue.

We will also verify a small number of grades in the field before they are set, so that the finished design rests on the ground as it actually stands and not on the survey alone. Any correction from that verification will be folded into the set before it is circulated for review.

The client review of the coordinated set is the one dependency outside our hands, and the schedule allows for a normal turnaround on it. If the comments come back promptly, the set moves to final and to seal without a pause; a longer review would push the sealed issue by the time it takes, and nothing else. We will send the coordinated copy as soon as it is clean, so the review can begin at the earliest point.

The work remains within the design fee of {{fact:f:E-2001-001.fee}}. Hours are being logged against the set as it progresses, and the effort spent to date is in line with the portion of the design that is complete. No additional services have been requested, and none are foreseen under the current scope.

items: Survey gaps: a small area at the north property line may still need a supplemental shot before final grading is set.
Coordination: the grading and roadway sheets must stay aligned as both advance; this is being managed by reviewing them together.
Client review turnaround: the schedule assumes comments on the coordinated set are returned promptly.
Site access and weather: field verification of any grade in question depends on access to the site.

blocks.text: Overall the design is on schedule and on budget, and the next step is to complete the grading set and prepare the coordinated review copy for the client. Prepared by Linda Nguyen, Design Technician.
